summary: Bitoku is a hand-management and worker-placement engine builder where players place spirit cards to gather resources and unlock abilities on a shared board, building toward multiple possible paths to victory. It's a fairly heavy, fiddly euro with strong production values and a lot of small interlocking bonuses to track.
praised: Satisfying engine building with multiple viable strategies
Attractive art and high production quality
Good solo mode for a game of this complexity
criticised: Fiddly bookkeeping with many small bonuses and exceptions to track
Dry, mechanical feel despite the fantasy theme
Rules overhead can slow down first plays significantly

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with some area majority
interaction.detail: Most of a player's engine — hand of yōkai cards, resources, and abilities — is private and built up largely independently of opponents. Interaction comes mainly from competing for shared worker-placement spots and area-majority scoring on the shared board rather than direct conflict.

sources: points from forest board space majorities
points from completed kodama or pilgrim sets
scoring.how_you_win: You play yōkai cards to place dice-workers around the forest board, building up area majorities, structures and card sets that score along the way and again at game end; the highest combined total wins.
